task.title: Background positioning and size
task.shortdesc: These CSS properties specify where a background image is placed, how large it is and which box is used as its positioning area.

info.p: “CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.7, Background Positioning Shorthand: the background-position shorthand property”.

Use background-position to specify each background image’s position inside its positioning area. A position can use keywords, lengths or percentages. With two values, the first sets the horizontal position and the second sets the vertical position.

The CSS initial value is 0% 0%, which places the image at the top-left. A percentage is calculated from the difference between the size of the positioning area and the size of the image. For example, 100% 100% aligns the image’s bottom-right corner with the area’s bottom-right corner.
“CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.6, Background Positioning: the background-position-x, background-position-y, background-position-inline, and background-position-block properties”.

Use these properties to specify a position on one axis. background-position-x and background-position-y use the physical horizontal and vertical axes. background-position-inline and background-position-block use the logical axes, which follow the element’s writing mode.
The physical properties use values such as left, right, top and bottom. The logical properties use start and end. Each also accepts center, a length or a percentage.
CSSMedia expands background-position into physical or logical axis values and also expands the background shorthand’s position.
“CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.10, Sizing Images: the background-size property”.

Use background-size to specify the width and height of each background image. Use one or two non-negative lengths or percentages. If you give one length or percentage, the other dimension defaults to auto.

auto uses the image’s intrinsic size or proportion. cover scales the image until it covers the positioning area, possibly cropping part of it. contain scales it until the whole image fits, possibly leaving part of the area uncovered. Separate sizes for multiple image layers with commas.
“CSS Backgrounds 4 §2.9, Positioning Area: the background-origin property”.
Use background-origin to specify the box that defines the positioning area for background images.

border-box uses the area inside the outer border edges, padding-box uses the area inside the outer padding edges, and content-box uses the content area. The CSS initial value is padding-box. This property does not affect an image whose background-attachment is fixed.
